title: Global Efficiency for the Continuous Napkin Functional via Growing-Spline Estimators
banked_reason: The final D-0.5 retry violated the approved finite-sample-only diagnostic scope and the reviewer found an unresolved causal/intervention-interpretation C-coherence defect.
gap_reasons: The asymptotic held-out certificate quantifies only over an integer M>K_n although K_n grows; it needs an explicit sequence M_n and growth conditions sufficient for covariance convergence on V_{M_n}^J.

The model class contains only observed-data laws satisfying a mean-Verma equality, but the proposal repeatedly concludes a Napkin intervention-mean/causal interpretation without declaring the required Napkin SCM or potential-outcome identification assumptions.
proof_attempt_summary: Eight D-0.5 proposal revisions successively repaired witness feasibility, source attribution, observed-law target definitions, and the restricted odd-h comparison, while preserving the proposed full-arm efficiency and growing-sieve attainment kernel. The final authorized retry deleted the asymptotic diagnostic theorem but retained forbidden population-certificate language and still overclaimed causal interpretation from an observed-law mean-Verma model, so discovery never passed D-0.5 and no Lean proof stage began.
tldr: The headline theorem gives a primitive cross-fitted growing-spline estimator for the observed-law target \(\tau(P)=c^{\top}\psi(P)\), with each \(\psi_x(P)\) defined by an explicit ratio of integrated g-formulas, that attains the full-arm continuous-Napkin efficiency bound and delivers uniform Wald coverage. The mean-Verma equality makes this functional equal to its \(z\)-invariant common cellwise Napkin intervention mean. Its asymptotic variance is strictly below that of every feasible prescribed finite weighting family whose certified omitted-direction residual is nonzero, with equality exactly at zero residual. The supporting geometry uses the coercive averaged-score operator \(C=M_D+T^{*}T\), and a separate fixed-\(S\), fixed-\(J\ge3\) theorem characterizes when zero-contrast arms strictly improve efficiency. A checked \(S=2,J=3\) odd-\(h\) law certifies nonemptiness under explicit envelope and Holder-radius compatibility conditions; its exact displayed gain concerns distinct optimizers restricted to \(\operatorname{span}\{1,h\}^3\), while unrestricted strictness follows from an explicitly nonzero omitted-direction residual. The unresolved theorem-level proof obligation is endpoint-safe finite-sample concentration for the cellwise learner at operator rate \(O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_n)\) without a \(K_n\) multiplier; failure of that rate is the kill condition.
gap: The continuous-\(Z\) Napkin literature gives locally optimal finite weighting combinations, and the general Verma literature gives abstract projection geometry, but no primitive growing-sieve estimator is known to attain the full-arm global bound.
fill: The headline result establishes primitive cross-fitted growing-sieve attainment and uniform Wald coverage for the explicit observed-law ratio-of-g-formulas target, with the mean-Verma restriction establishing its common cellwise causal interpretation and exact familywise strict dominance certified by omitted-direction residuals. Supporting results supply the full operator and bound, a general inactive-arm frontier, a separately verified three-arm witness whose finite-span gain and unrestricted residual arguments are kept distinct, the dimension-free perturbation and generated-score identity, and diagnostics that reveal omitted score directions.
